newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sydkraft 1996 profit seen 2.4 bln skr.
newsitem.headline: Sydkraft 1996 profit seen 2.4 bln skr.

text.p: Swedish utility company Sydkraft AB said on Friday it maintained its forecast for 1996 profit after net financial items of 2.4 billion crowns.

"The (forecast) result which was given at the time of the half-year report is unchanged -- a profit after financial items for 1996 of 2.4 billion crowns -- despite significantly lower hydro-electric power production," Sydkraft said in a statement.
Sydkraft posted a flat nine-month profit after financial items of 1.680 billion crowns compared to 1.684 in the same 1995 period. Turnover rose to 9.68 billion crowns from 8.65 billion.
"The lower result is due mainly to lower hydro-electric power production," it said.
It said financial items had fallen to a charge of 710 million crowns from a charge of 824 million because of a strong cash flow and lower interest rate costs.
"This was true despite an acquisition of 20 percent in (Swedish power producer and distributor) Graninge AB for around 1.8 billion crowns," the company said.
Turnover in Sydkraft's electricity division rose to 7.80 billion crowns from 6.85 billion, but operating profit fell to 1.86 billion crowns from 2.14 billion.

"The lower result compared with 1995 is mainly attributable to the cost of replacing the loss of 3.2 terawatt hours of hydroelectric power, combined with the fact that the market price of alternative power has increased...," it said.
Sydkraft said it produced 22,985 gigawatt hours of electricity during the first nine months of the year compared to 21,716 in the same 1995 period.
It said sales of electricity increased in part due to colder weather -- which accounted for an increase of two percent -- as well as a higher number of customers.
Hydroelectric power production fell because of low precipitation which has resulted in lower reservoir levels in the Nordic region.
Some 12,142 gigawatt hours of electricity was supplied by nuclear power compared to 11,294 gigawatt hours in the 1995 period.
Sydkraft said it bought 5,618 gigawatt hours of power from Denmark, Norway and Germany on the Norwegian-Swedish electricity exchange compared to 2,387 in the same 1995 period.
"The prices on the bourse have been high because of the dry situation," Sydkraft said.
